dedupe_keys.name: formation of the first internet exchange point in mexico interconnection lessons from the global south internet policy review 2021

description: This peer-reviewed analysis examines how the first Internet exchange point in Mexico was formed amid telecommunication reforms and asymmetric regulation in a market with low competition. It defines an IXP as a shared interconnection facility and a governance arena where technical and political dynamics mesh, shows that data centres, passive infrastructure and autonomous system numbers played a critical role given the lack of infrastructure in Mexico, and argues that an IXP's stability depends on its imagined affordances and on how the infrastructure, the telecommunications incumbent, its competitors, the regulator and the IXP operator interact, keeping the initiative in a fragile equilibrium. Producer: Fernanda R. Rosa (Department of Science, Technology, and Society, Virginia Tech), published on 2 November 2021 after review in January 2021, with funding from American University, Columbia University, Carnegie Corporation and R3D. Coverage: Mexico. Access: free open-access article. Licence and cost: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Germany, free. Caveats: a qualitative policy study without traffic or topology data. Simulation uses: it documents the institutional conditions and dependencies that agent-based and capacity models of IXP formation should represent. Related records: the ISOC assessment of IXP impact in Kenya and Nigeria (case_study-isoc-ixp-impact-kenya-nigeria-2012) and the Euro-IX IXP database (data-euro-ix-ixp-database).
